newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM leaves for Gore, Clinton meetings in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Russia PM leaves for Gore, Clinton meetings in U.S..

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin left Moscow on Wednesday for the United States, where he will meet President Bill Clinton and Vice-President Al Gore, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted a government spokesman as saying.
It said Chernomyrdin and Clinton would discuss the planned summit between Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin. No final date or location for the meeting has yet been set.

Under the Russian constitution Chernomyrdin would deputise for Yeltsin if Yeltsin was unable to complete his four-year term in office, running the country for three months until a new presidential election.
The talks with Gore, a regular session of the so-called U.S.-Russian Joint Commission on Economic and Technical Coooperation, are designed to foster trade and investment.

The spokesman said Chernomyrdin would stop in Shannon on his way to the U.S. to meet Ireland's Prime Minister John Bruton to discuss Russia's relationships with Ireland and the European Union. He would travel to Chicago from Washington to meet U.S. business leaders.
He is due to fly back to Moscow late on Saturday.
